question.text: Under the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956 (SCRA), derivatives are defined as:

answer.text: A security derived from a debt instrument, share, loan, risk instrument, or contract for differences or any other form of security
Only futures contracts on equity shares
Government bonds with variable interest rates

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 2(ac) of SCRA defines derivatives as a security derived from a debt instrument, share, loan whether secured or unsecured, risk instrument or contract for differences or any other form of security. A derivative also includes a contract which derives its value from the prices/index of prices of underlying securities. The Trap: Derivatives are broadly defined, not limited to equity futures only. The definition covers all types of derivatives including equity, interest rate, and other forms. Cross-Exam Context: The legal definition of derivatives under SCRA is a standard exam question. Distributor's Pro-Tip: Derivatives under SCRA: security derived from debt, shares, loans, risk instruments, or contracts for differences.
